---
title: "CAS PCPA Practice Project"
subtitle: "Iterative Model Refinement"

---

## Overview

In this video we make targeted model adjustments based on the diagnostic
findings from the previous video and recheck diagnostics after each
adjustment. We test each adjustment individually and retain changes that
improve model fit based on AICtweedie. The iterative nature of this
process reflects how model building works in practice.

---

1. Load Libraries and Data

Load tidyverse, statmod, and tweedie for modeling and diagnostics
```{r}
# install.packages("tidyverse")
# install.packages("statmod")
# install.packages("tweedie")
library(tidyverse)
library(statmod)
library(tweedie)

train   <- read_csv("train_residuals.csv")
model_D <- readRDS("model_D.rds")
p       <- readRDS("tweedie_p.rds")

cat("Using Tweedie p:", round(p, 4), "\n")
```

---

2. Re-apply Factor Levels

Re-apply factor levels since they are not preserved when saving to CSV
```{r}
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    gender            = factor(gender),
    marital_status    = factor(marital_status),
    coverage_type     = factor(coverage_type),
    value_band        = factor(value_band, levels = c("0-10k", "10k-20k", "20k-35k", "35k-50k", "50k+")),
    deductible        = factor(deductible),
    make              = factor(make),
    body_type         = factor(body_type),
    vehicle_use       = factor(vehicle_use),
    num_cylinders     = factor(num_cylinders),
    anti_theft_device = factor(anti_theft_device),
    safety_rating     = factor(safety_rating),
    region            = factor(region),
    urban_rural       = factor(urban_rural),
    tort_environment  = factor(tort_environment),
    catastrophe_risk  = factor(catastrophe_risk)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    gender            = relevel(gender, ref = "F"),
    marital_status    = relevel(marital_status, ref = "Married"),
    coverage_type     = relevel(coverage_type, ref = "Liability Only"),
    value_band        = relevel(value_band, ref = "10k-20k"),
    deductible        = relevel(deductible, ref = "500"),
    make              = relevel(make, ref = "Toyota"),
    body_type         = relevel(body_type, ref = "Sedan"),
    vehicle_use       = relevel(vehicle_use, ref = "Pleasure"),
    safety_rating     = relevel(safety_rating, ref = "3"),
    urban_rural       = relevel(urban_rural, ref = "Suburban"),
    tort_environment  = relevel(tort_environment, ref = "Moderate"),
    catastrophe_risk  = relevel(catastrophe_risk, ref = "Medium")
  )
```

---

3. Define Helper Functions

Create a function to print key fit statistics for any model
```{r}
model_summary <- function(model, label) {
  cat(label, "\n")
  cat("AIC:                 ", round(AICtweedie(model), 2), "\n")
  cat("% Deviance Explained:", round((1 - model$deviance / model$null.deviance) * 100, 2), "%\n")
  cat("\n")
}
```

Create a function to plot deviance residuals vs fitted values for
claimants only
```{r}
plot_resids <- function(model, data, title) {
  data %>%
    mutate(
      fitted_vals  = predict(model, type = "response"),
      deviance_res = residuals(model, type = "deviance")
    ) %>%
    filter(total_losses > 0) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = fitted_vals, y = deviance_res)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.3, color = "steelblue") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "darkgreen", se = FALSE) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x     = "Fitted Values",
      y     = "Deviance Residuals"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
}
```

---

4. Baseline Diagnostic Recap

Review Model D as the starting point before making any adjustments
```{r}
model_summary(model_D, "Model D (Baseline)")
```

Recheck the residual vs fitted plot
```{r}
train %>%
  filter(total_losses > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = fitted_values, y = deviance_resids)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "darkgreen", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Model D — Deviance Residuals vs Fitted Values (Claimants Only)",
    x     = "Fitted Values",
    y     = "Deviance Residuals"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Set the working model to Model D as the starting point
```{r}
model_working <- model_D
```

---

5. Adjustment 1 — violations_3yr x prior_claims_3yr Interaction

Violations and prior claims both capture driver risk history. Test
whether their interaction improves model fit — a driver with both high
violations and prior claims may represent compounding risk that a
linear additive model does not capture.
```{r}
formula_viol_claims <- paste(
  paste(deparse(formula(model_working)), collapse = " "),
  "+ violations_3yr:prior_claims_3yr"
)

model_viol_claims <- glm(
  as.formula(formula_viol_claims),
  data   = train,
  family = tweedie(var.power = p, link.power = 0)
)

cat("Working model AIC:                            ", round(AICtweedie(model_working), 2), "\n")
cat("With violations:prior_claims interaction AIC: ", round(AICtweedie(model_viol_claims), 2), "\n")
```

Check residual plot after adding the interaction
```{r}
plot_resids(model_viol_claims, train,
            "With violations:prior_claims Interaction (Claimants Only)")
```

Update working model if interaction improves AIC
```{r}
if (AICtweedie(model_viol_claims) < AICtweedie(model_working)) {
  model_working <- model_viol_claims
  cat("Interaction retained — AIC improved\n")
} else {
  cat("Interaction not retained — no AIC improvement\n")
}
```

---

6. Adjustment 2 — prior_claims_3yr as a Factor

Prior claims is discrete and low-valued (0, 1, 2, 3+). Treating it
as continuous assumes equal jumps between levels. Converting to a factor
allows each level to have its own coefficient and may better capture
the nonlinear effect particularly the large jump from 0 to 1 claim.

Create prior claims factor variable
```{r}
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    prior_claims_fct = factor(
      case_when(
        prior_claims_3yr == 0 ~ "0",
        prior_claims_3yr == 1 ~ "1",
        prior_claims_3yr == 2 ~ "2",
        prior_claims_3yr >= 3 ~ "3+"
      ),
      levels = c("0", "1", "2", "3+")
    )
  )
```

Fit model replacing continuous prior_claims_3yr with factor version
```{r}
formula_prior_fct <- gsub(
  "prior_claims_3yr",
  "prior_claims_fct",
  paste(deparse(formula(model_working)), collapse = " ")
)

model_prior_fct <- glm(
  as.formula(formula_prior_fct),
  data   = train,
  family = tweedie(var.power = p, link.power = 0)
)

cat("Working model AIC:                    ", round(AICtweedie(model_working), 2), "\n")
cat("With prior_claims as factor AIC:      ", round(AICtweedie(model_prior_fct), 2), "\n")
```

Review factor level coefficients to assess whether the relationship
is truly nonlinear
```{r}
summary(model_prior_fct)$coefficients[grepl("prior_claims_fct", rownames(summary(model_prior_fct)$coefficients)), ]
```

Check residual plot
```{r}
plot_resids(model_prior_fct, train,
            "With prior_claims as Factor (Claimants Only)")
```

Update working model if factor form improves AIC
```{r}
if (AICtweedie(model_prior_fct) < AICtweedie(model_working)) {
  model_working <- model_prior_fct
  cat("prior_claims factor retained — AIC improved\n")
} else {
  cat("prior_claims factor not retained — no AIC improvement\n")
}
```

---

7. Adjustment 3 — violations_3yr as a Factor

Same reasoning as prior claims — violations is discrete and low-valued.
Converting to a factor allows the model to capture potential nonlinearity
in the violations effect.

Create violations factor variable
```{r}
train <- train %>%
  mutate(
    violations_fct = factor(
      case_when(
        violations_3yr == 0 ~ "0",
        violations_3yr == 1 ~ "1",
        violations_3yr == 2 ~ "2",
        violations_3yr >= 3 ~ "3+"
      ),
      levels = c("0", "1", "2", "3+")
    )
  )
```

Fit model replacing continuous violations_3yr with factor version
```{r}
formula_viol_fct <- gsub(
  "violations_3yr",
  "violations_fct",
  paste(deparse(formula(model_working)), collapse = " ")
)

model_viol_fct <- glm(
  as.formula(formula_viol_fct),
  data   = train,
  family = tweedie(var.power = p, link.power = 0)
)

cat("Working model AIC:                    ", round(AICtweedie(model_working), 2), "\n")
cat("With violations as factor AIC:        ", round(AICtweedie(model_viol_fct), 2), "\n")
```

Review factor level coefficients
```{r}
summary(model_viol_fct)$coefficients[grepl("violations_fct", rownames(summary(model_viol_fct)$coefficients)), ]
```

Check residual plot
```{r}
plot_resids(model_viol_fct, train,
            "With violations as Factor (Claimants Only)")
```

Update working model if factor form improves AIC
```{r}
if (AICtweedie(model_viol_fct) < AICtweedie(model_working)) {
  model_working <- model_viol_fct
  cat("violations factor retained — AIC improved\n")
} else {
  cat("violations factor not retained — no AIC improvement\n")
}
```

---

8. Adjustment 4 — gender x urban_rural Interaction

Young males in urban areas are known to have disproportionately higher
loss costs than either risk factor alone would suggest. Test whether
this interaction improves model fit.
```{r}
formula_gender_urban <- paste(
  paste(deparse(formula(model_working)), collapse = " "),
  "+ gender:urban_rural"
)

model_gender_urban <- glm(
  as.formula(formula_gender_urban),
  data   = train,
  family = tweedie(var.power = p, link.power = 0)
)

cat("Working model AIC:                       ", round(AICtweedie(model_working), 2), "\n")
cat("With gender:urban_rural interaction AIC: ", round(AICtweedie(model_gender_urban), 2), "\n")
```

Check residual plot
```{r}
plot_resids(model_gender_urban, train,
            "With gender:urban_rural Interaction (Claimants Only)")
```

Update working model if interaction improves AIC
```{r}
if (AICtweedie(model_gender_urban) < AICtweedie(model_working)) {
  model_working <- model_gender_urban
  cat("gender:urban_rural interaction retained — AIC improved\n")
} else {
  cat("gender:urban_rural interaction not retained — no AIC improvement\n")
}
```

---

9. Re-profile Tweedie p on the Best Model

Now that variable selection and refinement are complete re-profile the
Tweedie p on the working model to confirm the original estimate is still
appropriate. The optimal p may shift slightly with a different predictor
set.
```{r}
# install.packages("tweedie")
p_recheck <- tweedie.profile(
  formula(model_working),
  p.vec   = seq(1.1, 1.9, by = 0.1),
  data    = train,
  do.plot = TRUE,
  method  = "series"
)

cat("Original p:   ", round(p, 4), "\n")
cat("Re-profiled p:", round(p_recheck$p.max, 4), "\n")
```

Refine the new p estimate over a narrower range
```{r}
p_new <- p_recheck$p.max

p_refined <- tweedie.profile(
  formula(model_working),
  p.vec   = seq(p_new - 0.1, p_new + 0.1, by = 0.01),
  data    = train,
  do.plot = TRUE,
  method  = "series"
)

p_final <- p_refined$p.max
cat("Final re-profiled p:", round(p_final, 4), "\n")
```

---

10. Refit Final Model with New p

Refit the working model using the re-profiled p value
```{r}
model_final <- glm(
  formula(model_working),
  data   = train,
  family = tweedie(var.power = p_final, link.power = 0)
)
```

---

11. AIC Comparison — Model D vs Final Model

Compare the final model against Model D across key metrics
```{r}
cat("=== Model Comparison ===\n\n")
cat("Model D AIC:     ", round(AICtweedie(model_D), 2), "\n")
cat("Final Model AIC: ", round(AICtweedie(model_final), 2), "\n\n")
cat("Model D % Deviance Explained:     ",
    round((1 - model_D$deviance / model_D$null.deviance) * 100, 2), "%\n")
cat("Final Model % Deviance Explained: ",
    round((1 - model_final$deviance / model_final$null.deviance) * 100, 2), "%\n\n")
cat("Original Tweedie p:    ", round(p, 4), "\n")
cat("Re-profiled Tweedie p: ", round(p_final, 4), "\n")
```

Final residual plot to confirm improvement
```{r}
plot_resids(model_final, train,
            "Final Model — Deviance Residuals vs Fitted Values (Claimants Only)")
```

---

12. Save the Final Model

Save the final model and updated p value
```{r}
saveRDS(model_final, "model_final.rds")
saveRDS(p_final, "tweedie_p_final.rds")
cat("Final model saved to model_final.rds\n")
cat("Final p saved to tweedie_p_final.rds\n")
```

---

## Key Observations

- Each adjustment was tested individually using AICtweedie as the selection criterion — a lower AIC indicates a better balance of fit and complexity
- The violations x prior_claims interaction tests whether compounding driver risk is captured better by an interaction term than by additive effects alone
- Converting prior_claims and violations to factors allows the model to capture nonlinear jumps between levels — particularly the disproportionately large effect of going from zero to one claim or violation
- The gender x urban_rural interaction tests whether the risk differential between genders is amplified in urban areas
- Re-profiling Tweedie p after variable refinement confirms whether the distributional assumption remains appropriate with the final predictor set
- The final AIC comparison against Model D documents the overall improvement from the iterative refinement process
